        # after a word: 'that much' (那么 + adjective), strong;
        # at the start of a clause: 'then', weak
        value = 3.0 if (not last or last in PUNCTUATION) else 8.5
    elif tok in DEGREE or any(d in tok for d in ("这么", "那么", "这麽", "那麽", "这麼", "那麼")):
        value = 9.0
    elif tok in MO:
        value = 11.0 if last in DEMONSTRATIVE else 2.0
    elif tok == "般":
        value = 8.0 if last in DEMONSTRATIVE else 1.5
    elif tok in MANNER:
        value = 1.8
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, value

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:4412 — the preposition "for" (and its translations).

What it does: this direction of the MLP output fires on the word "for" when it is used as a
preposition in running text ("cooked for 20 minutes", "a tool for hikers", "for the day"),
and on the same word in other languages ("pour", "para", "für", "por", "за", "для", "za").
It is strongest on "за"/"za" (Russian/Polish "for"), then "pour", "sau", "für", "para".
It stays near zero on "for" used as a Python/C loop keyword (at the start of an indented
line), and it is weaker on "for" after verbs of looking or waiting ("look for", "waiting
for"). "over" in duration phrases ("over two hours") gives a smaller response. Everything
else is predicted as 0.

The numbers are the average activation per word, measured on training text.
"""

# Average activation of each "for"-like word when it is used as a preposition.
FOR_WORDS = {
    " for": 1.5, "for": 1.0, " For": 0.9, "For": 0.9, " FOR": 1.5, "_FOR": 1.7, "_for": 1.0,
    "-for": 1.6, " over": 0.8, " per": 0.65,
    " pour": 2.0, " para": 1.3, " Para": 1.4, " für": 1.3, " Für": 1.3, " por": 0.6,
    " pra": 1.1, " sau": 2.4, " для": 1.0, " за": 8.0, " za": 9.9, " Za": 2.5,
}

# Verbs after which "for" means "in search of" or "in expectation of", not a purpose.
SEARCH_WORDS = {"look", "looking", "looked", "wait", "waiting", "search", "searching"}

READS = ()


def line_starts_here(strings, t):
    """True if only indentation comes before token t on its line (a code-style line start)."""
    for j in range(t - 1, -1, -1):
        s = strings[j]
        if "\n" in s:
            return s.split("\n")[-1].strip() == ""
        if s.strip():
            return False
    return True


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    t = len(strings) - 1
    word = strings[t]
    value = FOR_WORDS.get(word, 0.0)
    if word == " for" and line_starts_here(strings, t):
        value = 0.0  # a Python/C loop keyword such as "for x in ..."
    if word in (" for", "for") and t > 0 and strings[t - 1].strip().lower() in SEARCH_WORDS:
        value *= 0.3
    return carry, value

"""A coarse boundary/composition signal, not a semantic topic detector.

Punctuation and grammatical words respond more than ordinary content words.
Their shared context score falls when the preceding 16/64 tokens contain many
letters, newlines, or title-cased tokens. Each token class has a small baseline,
context sensitivity, and a correction that decays from the document's start.
These are fitted broad averages; most native contextual variation is missing.
"""
from collections import deque

READS = ()
LETTERS, NEWLINES, TITLE_CASE = range(3)

# (baseline, document-start correction, sensitivity to recent composition)
WORD_CLASSES = (
    # Copula
    ("am is are was were", (-.088, .515, .145)),
    # Other auxiliaries and modals
    ("be been being has have had do does did can could will would shall "
     "should may might must", (-.013, .295, .085)),
    # Additive/adversative conjunctions, then alternatives
    ("and but yet nor", (-.110, .355, .132)),
    ("or", (.072, .169, .016)),
    # Articles and demonstratives
    ("a an the", (.008, -.103, .135)),
    ("this that these those", (-.037, .245, .121)),
    # Personal pronouns and possessives
    ("i me my mine we us our ours you your yours he him his she her hers "
     "it its they them their theirs", (.012, .376, .080)),
    # Prepositions
    ("of to in on at by for from with as into over under through out off "
     "about after before between during without within against",
     (.010, .286, .048)),
    # Subordinating and relative connectors
    ("if when while although though because since unless until whether "
     "which who whom whose where than", (-.030, .018, .105)),
)
GRAMMAR = {word: values for words, values in WORD_CLASSES
           for word in words.split()}


def token_class(s):
    word = s.strip()
    if "\n\n" in s:
        return .023, -.141, .317
    if "\n" in s:
        return -.090, .552, .151
    if s.isspace():
        # Nonbreaking spaces differ from ordinary spacing in the training data.
        if "\xa0" in s:
            return .28, 0., 0.
        return -.073, .334, .114
    if word and all(c in ",;:，；：" for c in word):
        return -.109, .268, .110
    if word and all(c in ".!?。！？" for c in word):
        return -.055, .202, .147
    if word and all(c in "()[]{}（）【】" for c in word):
        return -.056, .185, .102
    if word and not any(c.isalnum() for c in word):
        return -.027, .067, .114
    if word.lower() in GRAMMAR:
        return GRAMMAR[word.lower()]
    if word.isalpha():
        return -.004, .307, .013
    if word.isdigit():
        return -.021, -.099, .027
    return -.016, .472, .013


class Recent:
    """Rolling counts of letters, newline characters and title-cased tokens."""
    def __init__(self, length):
        self.length = length
        self.tokens = deque()
        self.totals = [0., 0., 0.]

    def mean(self, feature):
        return self.totals[feature] / max(1, len(self.tokens))

    def add(self, counts):
        self.tokens.append(counts)
        for i in range(3):
            self.totals[i] += counts[i]
        if len(self.tokens) > self.length:
            old = self.tokens.popleft()
            for i in range(3):
                self.totals[i] -= old[i]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, Recent(16), Recent(64))
    _, position, short, long = carry
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    context = (
        1.598 - .233 * short.mean(LETTERS) - .277 * long.mean(LETTERS)
        - 2.025 * short.mean(NEWLINES) - 1.525 * short.mean(TITLE_CASE)
    )
    baseline, start, sensitivity = token_class(s)
    value = baseline + start / (position + 1) + sensitivity * context
    counts = (sum(c.isalpha() for c in s), s.count("\n"),
              float(s.strip().istitle()))
    short.add(counts)
    long.add(counts)
    return (doc, position + 1, short, long), float(value)

"""Layer-1 MLP down-projection, component 4414 (weak and diffuse).

What it does, in plain terms. Inside running English prose the component leans negative:
on commas and other mid-sentence punctuation, on clause-joining words ("and", "but", "is",
"has", "this", "that", "The"), and on line-ending punctuation. It leans positive at the
closing of a parenthesis or sentence ("). ", ").", ".\n\n") and on a few other words
("I", "or", "by", "on"). It is clearly positive on the first token of a document, and
shifted up when the recent text looks like maths or code (digits, '=', brackets, operators).
Most of its variance comes from context this program does not model, so these are rough
offsets, not precise predictions.
"""

import re

MATH = re.compile(r"[=+*^/\\$()\[\]{}<>]|\d")
CJK = re.compile(r"[一-鿿]")
WORD = re.compile(r" ?[A-Za-z]+")
PUNCT_MID = re.compile(r"\s?[,;:，、；：]")
PUNCT_END = re.compile(r"\s?[.?!。？！]")
DIGITS = re.compile(r"\s?\d+")

JOINERS = frozenset("and but is has are this that the so if can will for my".split())
CLOSERS = frozenset(["). ", ").", "),", ".\n\n", " I", " or", " by", " on"])

INTERCEPT = -0.04
FIRST_TOKEN = 0.37  # first token of a document
MATH_WEIGHT = 0.10  # per unit of maths/code density in the last 30 tokens
WINDOW = 30


def kind_offset(s):
    """Offset for one token, from what kind of text it is."""
    if s in CLOSERS:
        return 0.11
    if s.strip().lower() in JOINERS and s.startswith(" ") or s == "The":
        return -0.09
    if "\n" in s:
        return -0.02
    if s.strip() == "":
        return -0.02
    if PUNCT_MID.fullmatch(s):
        return -0.07
    if PUNCT_END.fullmatch(s):
        return -0.01
    if CJK.search(s):
        return 0.03
    if DIGITS.fullmatch(s):
        return 0.0
    if WORD.fullmatch(s):
        return 0.03
    return 0.02


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """carry: (document id, the last tokens of this document); None at a row's start."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    recent = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else []
    first = len(recent) == 0
    window = (recent + [s])[-WINDOW:]
    math_density = sum(bool(MATH.search(w)) for w in window) / len(window)
    value = INTERCEPT + kind_offset(s) + MATH_WEIGHT * math_density
    value += FIRST_TOKEN if first else 0.0
    return (doc, window), float(value)
